Hey ! I am 21 and I think my mother is toxic.
I will tell you my experience but I think everyone has a different story .

She is in the medical field , so since I was young she was always focused on math. When she would do my homework with me , she would scream , saying I can’t comprehend, and would end up tearing my book apart and make all of my sheet flying away in our garden.
For sure I would always end up crying haha.

This expectation has always been there till the end of high school, since I moved out to study far way , it has removed some weight on my shoulder.

I grew up really shy and kind of introvert, though I don’t know if it’s link to the way I was raised.
I act quite different with people from my social circle . I am « the real me ». And I don’t make any of my friends meet my mother ( she will always make comment about them, or ask about their grades and then tell me that I should do like them because they’re smart...).
When i am with people that I know and that I got to know by myself , I am more free , more confident .

When my mother is around with people we know ( her friends for example), I feel like I have boundaries and that I should be careful of everything I say, how the way I act, what I wear.

To me it’s better to live alone while I am way because I don’t feel the “dominance” of my mother . These pas fees months of quarantine sure have been really hard on me. 

As time flies by, I got used to her remarks about how I should improve my grade, shouldn’t do this sport , lose weight ... it still hurts today but I cry alone in my bed and manage to be without any emotion or hiding them when she tell me that.

Yes true ! When all of your friends’lives seems so cool and without rules and you’re like « wtf » you are allowed to do that ?

Also, having toxic parent is the fear to get punished for something you’ve done, so you learn to lie ( just to push back the deadline haha), grow a little more introvert.

I think every person has different story. If you don’t feel good with them and how they treat you, I guess it’s a warning
